result.keywords: Autonomous underwater vehicle mission execution requires reliable path following under hydrodynamic uncertainty, actuator limits, and environmental disturbance. This paper presents a cooperative path-following control strategy for AUVs that combines particle swarm optimization (PSO) with radial basis function (RBF) compensation. PSO is used to search for feasible waypoint sequences and tune control parameters, while an RBF-based estimator compensates for nonlinear model errors and improves trajectory smoothness. A coordinated control structure is developed to reduce collision risk and enhance tracking accuracy in constrained underwater environments. Simulation results indicate improved convergence speed, lower tracking error, and stronger robustness compared with conventional planning and control methods.
result.title: Cooperative path-following control for autonomous underwater vehicles using particle swarm optimization and radial basis function compensation
